correctness.rationale: Exact complete enumeration of all (n!)^(2n) labeled strict preference profiles for n=1,2,3, every n! perfect matching and every blocking pair, with two independent implementations of blocking criterion. Among exactly 46,656 n=3 profiles and 14,760 unordered stable-matching pairs, all 8,304 distinct-cost pairs show strictly opposite Nash-product order. Histograms 43,728 equal and 2,928 strict Nash subset are exact; a four-pair 24-matching enumeration produces precisely the two stable matchings and the scores 7/4096 versus 8/4608. All computations use exact integers; checked executable artifact included.

value.rationale: The 2026 Nash stable-marriage proposal explicitly benchmarks egalitarian fairness. The strongest possible strict ordering of any two stable alternatives up to n=3, and the first size n=4 at which it reverses, identify a natural exact structural boundary with direct implications for whether one fairness score can replace the other. The 2928/46656 tie-refinement incidence differentiates selection among equal egalitarian outcomes from genuine conflicting choices. Neither a routine substitution nor an unmotivated slice: market size is the minimal dimension at which the practical objectives can become incompatible.
